project.title: Spooky Monopoly
project.summary: A single-player browser property game with local token unlocks and optional shared statistics.

items.title: Verify a clean dependency install and production run
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). In a fresh checkout with Node.js 22 or later and pnpm 12, run install, typecheck, build and start. Record the versions and address any lockfile or setup issues found. Run this first so the other checks start from a reproducible production build.

items.title: Check the original event URLs alongside the root routes
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). Cover the game page, GET stats, and POST submit at both URL forms. Verify that the aliases retain the handler methods and response behaviour. Check next.config.ts and both route families against the production server, including the expected responses with Supabase absent.

items.title: Add a regression check for the local game flow
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). With Supabase settings absent, cover token selection, a property choice, the end-of-game summary after 20 turns, and restart. Use a fixed roll sequence. Cover purchase, pass, resolution of owned and special spaces, an unaffordable vampire landing, and the last turn. Capture baseline money and ownership outcomes before changing the turn controls.

items.title: Make the full game playable on phones and tablets
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). Update GameBoard.css, GameSidebar.tsx, GameSidebar.css, and TokenPicker.css to keep the board, turn, cash, current space, and Roll action reachable. Move the intro and full log into expandable sections at narrow widths. Add text labels for active and owned spaces, visible focus, 44 CSS-pixel primary targets, and at least 4.5:1 contrast for primary button text. Verify 320px and 390px widths and tablet landscape.

items.title: Make property decisions faster and explicit
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). In GameBoard.tsx and PropertyPopup.tsx, reserve purchase decision controls for actionable choices. Give options short labels such as Buy for $60 or Pass, with faction flavour underneath. Confirm the intended vampire purchase rule before changing dismissal. Route clicks, keyboard actions, and dismissal through the same legal-action checks, including a clear continuation when purchase is unaffordable. Manage dialog focus and return it after the decision. Compare fixed-roll outcomes with the baseline.

items.title: Explain faction rules and surface earned unlocks
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). Give tokens readable faction names and a one-line play rule in TokenPicker.tsx. Explain how each locked faction becomes available and confirm newly earned unlocks in EndGame.tsx before restart.

items.title: Add regression coverage for browser token unlocks
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). Cover a fresh browser origin, a qualifying unlock, and the token selection available after restart and reload in the same origin. Verify that the newly unlocked faction is explained in the results and available in the picker on restart and reload.

items.title: Distinguish empty, unconfigured, and failed statistics
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). In GlobalStats.tsx, explain why shared results are unavailable or empty, and offer retry for transient failures. Keep the local result and restart control usable while statistics are loading or unavailable.

items.title: Cover unavailable and empty statistics states
items.notes: Phase 1 (Now). Distinguish missing configuration and database errors from a successful zero-game response. Verify the game summary and restart remain available. Use fixtures for the zero-game response, missing configuration, and a transient failure and recovery.

items.title: Verify the results flow against a configured Supabase project
items.notes: Phase 2 (Next). Use a test project with the existing table contract. Verify an empty aggregate, one completed-game insert, and the resulting totals and token-group counts under the public-key policies. Verify live table constraints and policies before changing shared writes or aggregation. Keep local play independent of this check.

items.title: Validate submissions and show confirmed aggregates
items.notes: Phase 2 (Next). Validate result fields at runtime in the submit handler. Introduce a backward-compatible submission ID and a database uniqueness rule once the live schema is confirmed. Check HTTP responses in EndGame.tsx and refresh GlobalStats.tsx after a confirmed submission. Verify aggregates across response pages and confirm that a failed or retried submission leaves local play available.

items.title: Resume an interrupted run in the same browser
items.notes: Phase 2 (Next). Save a versioned snapshot after committed game actions using stable token and board identifiers. Restore turn, position, cash, owned properties, and any unresolved property choice without repeating a charge. Offer Resume and Start new, with a safe fallback for incompatible or corrupt saves.

items.title: Export a shareable card from a completed game
items.notes: Phase 2 (Next). Use the end-game title, faction, achievements, cash, and property totals to generate a downloadable image and copyable text for Discord or group chats. Verify the export works without Supabase or a connected account.

items.title: Share repeatable challenges using a seeded run
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Extract deterministic turn rules from GameBoard.tsx and keep rules randomness separate from animation. A challenge link identifies the seed, faction, and rules or board version. Identical legal actions in two fresh browser profiles should produce the same terminal state. Explain unsupported rules versions.

items.title: Compare an alternate property decision in Ghost Ledger
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Build on deterministic challenges and structured turn inputs. From EndGame.tsx, let the player change one legal property decision and replay under the same random inputs. Show cash and ownership timelines side by side and flag the first later action that becomes illegal. Verify that replaying the original actions reproduces the actual result.

items.title: Define and test the two-seat match rules
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 1 (supervised two-player pilot). Record the contract in docs/multiplayer-rules.md before changing the engine. Prototype equal human seats, random first seat, and 10 rounds with one turn per player per round. Define legal Buy and Pass actions for unowned properties. Test posted rent transferred to the owner on landing, capped by the payer’s cash, with both players remaining through the last round. Score cash plus owned property purchase value and allow ties. Include worked examples for unaffordable rent, a purchase, and a tie. Playtest first-seat advantage before tuning rent and pacing.

items.title: Resolve shared turns on the server
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 1 (supervised two-player pilot). After define-two-seat-match-rules and the solo legal-choice fixes, extract deterministic turn rules from GameBoard.tsx and PropertyPopup.tsx. Reuse the rules foundation with seeded challenges. Challenge-link UI and Ghost Ledger are independent. Keep solo regression fixtures for balances, purchases, and unlocks. In multiplayer, accept a player intent with an action ID and expected room revision, validate the acting seat and legal action, and resolve randomness, transfers, ownership, and turn advancement in a single commit. Verify duplicate, stale, and wrong-seat actions cannot apply a second move.

items.title: Let two players join a private match by invite
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 1 (supervised two-player pilot). Prototype host and guest views with fixture data in GameSidebar.tsx and GameBoard.css at phone widths. Add a Play with a friend entry, shareable invite link, editable default seat names, and Ready controls. Give occupied seats credentials separate from the invite. Verify a client without a seat cannot read or act in the room and a member of one room cannot access another room.

items.title: Persist and synchronise shared match state
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 1 (supervised two-player pilot). Build on add-authoritative-turn-engine and add-private-invite-rooms. Persist rooms, members, accepted action IDs, revisions, and the latest snapshot separately from solo statistics. Start with short foreground polling and an immediate refresh on action, tab return, or reconnect. Keep the last confirmed board visible while a write is pending. Verify both clients finish a match with equal state and waiting clients reflect accepted actions within three seconds at the 95th percentile on a stable test connection. Consider push updates if polling misses the target.

items.title: Make shared turns easy to follow on small screens
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 1 (supervised two-player pilot). Build on the compact solo layout and fixture-based lobby prototype. Adapt GameBoard.tsx and GameSidebar.tsx for active and waiting views, overlapping tokens, and ownership labels that work without colour. Give the active player a reachable turn dock with legal actions, current space, and named turn status. Closing property details must keep the choice pending. Verify 320 CSS-pixel width, 44 CSS-pixel primary targets, and a complete keyboard turn.

items.title: Restore player seats and handle abandoned matches
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 2 (private release). Build on the persisted room snapshot and seat credential. Restore the current revision and pending decision after refresh, disconnect, or backgrounding. Test recovery from a write committed before the connection dropped. Show who is away and give the waiting player a visible grace period and the option to end an abandoned match when it expires. Provide an explicit Leave match action. Abandonment must end once, award no competitive result, and make no purchase or pass on an absent player’s behalf.

items.title: Add multiplayer games with shared turns
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 2 (private release). Release the private two-player mode once the supervised pilot, authoritative turns, phone-sized board, and reconnect and leave flow are verified. Two separate browser profiles must join, reconnect, and finish the same match without duplicate turns or divergent results. Preserve standalone solo play and keep multiplayer results separate from solo aggregates. Measure invite-to-first-roll time, pilot completion, and the share of interrupted matches that resume to completion.

items.title: Export a recap of a finished multiplayer match
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 2 (private release). Build on the planned solo result card and the finalised multiplayer result. Generate a downloadable image and copyable text with the outcome, seat names or initials, and verified highlights. Exclude room credentials and invite links. Both players should be able to export the same result. Measure recap exports among finished matches.

items.title: Support private matches for three to four players
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 3 (expansion). Build on the private two-seat release. Extend the seat model and layout, then playtest equal seats at each room size before changing faction rules. Check wait time, competition for property, and round count. Verify all four seats receive the intended number of turns and a reconnect restores the same seat. Compare match completion by room size.

items.title: Make faction differences playable in multiplayer
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 3 (expansion). Use the equal-seat baseline and larger-room playtests before introducing faction variants. Document legal actions and objectives before match start. Test vampire acquisition advantages and an elf objective that recognises resistance rather than relying on the standard wealth score. Verify each enabled faction has a reachable objective and keep equal-seat play available.

items.title: Show the shared history of rent and ownership
items.notes: Phase 3 (Later). Multiplayer stage 3 (expansion). Build on stable player and property IDs and the recorded action history. Highlight actual rent transfers, later purchases, and changes in ownership. Distinguish observed transfers from illustrative links about how pooled cash funded another action. Verify the recap matches recorded transactions and final balances and is readable on a phone. Measure rematches after players view the result.
